newsitem.title: INDIA: Former Indian minister arrested at airport.
newsitem.headline: Former Indian minister arrested at airport.

text.p: Indian police arrested a former government minister wanted in a corruption case stemming from the discovery of more than $1 million in cash stashed in his homes, the Press Trust of India (PTI) reported on Tuesday.
Former communications minister Sukh Ram was arrested by federal police at New Delhi's international airport late on Monday after he arrived in the Indian capital on a flight from London, PTI said.
Sukh Ram was out of the country last month when Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) agents raided his homes.
He has denied the corruption accusations and said he was seeking medical treatment overseas.
CBI officials were not immediately available for comment.

Sukh Ram is wanted for questioning by federal investigators and must appear before a local judge by October 1 under the terms of the arrest warrant, officials said. A court issued the warrant on Monday.

Sukh Ram served in the cabinet of former prime minister P.V. Narasimha Rao, whose Congress party was beaten in general elections which ended in May. He spearheaded an ambitious drive to end the government's monopoly over telephone services.
The CBI has accused him of pocketing kickbacks from a private firm which sold the government radio equipment, but the federal police agency has not filed any formal charges.
Sukh Ram has denied accusations of corruption stemming from the discovery of some 36 million rupees ($1 million) in cash stuffed in suitcases and bags in two houses in New Delhi and nearby Ghaziabad.

"It was part of funds raised by the (Congress) party for electioneering," PTI quoted Sukh Ram on Monday as saying in London. "The money had been given to me by an important party functionary for party use in the election campaign to the Uttar Pradesh assembly."
Uttar Pradesh, India's most populous state, holds assembly elections starting on September 30.
But the Congress party, which suspended Sukh Ram after the raids, has said the seized money did not belong to it.

The raids on Sukh Ram's homes marked the latest in a series of scandals that have hit the Congress party this year and which opinion polls have shown contributed to its defeat in the general elections.
